newsitem.title: LATVIA: ELECTRONIC TRADE TO BE LAUNCHED ON BOURSE IN JUNE.
newsitem.headline: ELECTRONIC TRADE TO BE LAUNCHED ON BOURSE IN JUNE.

text.p: The Riga stock exchange said on Tuesday that it will enter the late twentieth century and provide electronic trade facilities to dealers from early June.

"We will provide the service of accepting, selling and buying orders from dealers electronically starting in the first half of June," Armins Kalninsh, head of the bourse's settlement and trading department, told Reuters.
"We will introduce the service gradually, as more phone lines come to be available," Kalninsh said.
"Virtually all dealers have expressed an interest (in the service)," Kalninsh added. "This is only natural as it saves time."
Currently dealers have to bring the orders to the bourse in person for both the reopening and the noon session.
Kalninsh said that the electronic service would consign hand delivery to the dust-bin of market history and enable brokers to cut deals from their offices.
"For these purposes we will use software similar to that currently applied in Lithuania, as well as Poland and the Czech Republic," Kalninsh said.
